product.description: Marea Britanie a acordat independența Egiptului, iar țara are o Constituție proprie. Totuși, pe teritoriul țării staționează încă trupe britanice a căror prezență nu lasă rănile sufletești să se vindece. Familia Abd el-Gawad este îndurerată de pierderea lui Fahmi, cel mai bun dintre fii. Kamal, mezinul familiei, a ajuns la vârsta marilor decizii, dar și a primei iubiri. Pentru el, dragostea îmbracă o formă pură, incompatibilă cu realitățile vieții. Idealismul tânărului se confruntă timpuriu cu decepțiile: iubita, ca orice femeie, se căsătorește; eroii naționaliști se aliază la guvernare cu cei considerați trădători ai cauzei naționale; credința profundă, care rezistase în fața asaltului influențelor occidentale, se prăbușește sub noile adevăruri ale științei și umanismului.   Prin personajele sale, Naghib Mahfuz merge pe străzile orașului Cairo și urmărește călătoria fascinantă a culturii islamice către noutățile lumii moderne. Palatul dorinței desfășoară în fața cititorilor o poveste ca un arabesc, creând în același timp orizontul de așteptare pentru următorul roman, Strada Zahărului. Paul E. Hutchinson

## Discover *Palatul dorintei* (The Palace of Desire)

Immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of modern Egyptian life with *Palatul dorintei*. This seminal work by Naguib Mahfouz offers readers a profound, sweeping journey through the culture and changing times of Cairo. It is an essential read for those interested in Arabic literature, modernist fiction, and historical narratives that capture the spirit of a city at a crossroads.

The story unfolds against a backdrop of intense social change following Britain's granting of Egyptian independence. Although sovereignty was achieved, the lingering presence of British troops casts a shadow over the nation's heart, affecting every deep emotional wound. The novel centers on the Abd el-Gawad family, whose lives are touched by loss and profound shifts in personal identity.

## A Narrative of Love, Idealism, and Change

*Palatul dorintei* follows Kamal, a man who has reached a pivotal ageâa time for great decisions, but also defining moments of first love. For him, love manifests as something pure, seemingly incompatible with the harsh realities of life. His youthful idealism is constantly tested: his beloved marries another; national heroes align themselves with those viewed as traitors to the cause; and even deep-seated religious faith struggles against the new truths offered by Western science and humanism.

Naguib Mahfouz guides us through the bustling streets of Cairo, creating a fascinating portrayal of Islamic culture navigating the currents of modern global influences. The novel is structured like an exquisite arabesque, drawing the reader into its complexity while simultaneously building immense anticipation for his subsequent masterpiece, *The Sugar Street*.

### Why Read This Literary Classic?

*Palatul dorintei* offers more than just a story; it provides a cultural mirror. It allows readers to witness how tradition clashes with modernity, and how personal desires intersect with massive historical forces in 20th-century Egypt. Paul E. Hutchinson brings this masterful narrative to life for contemporary audiences.

---

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**What is *Palatul dorintei* about?**
It is a complex fictional novel set in Cairo, exploring themes of love, societal change, idealism, and the struggle between tradition and modernity in post-independence Egypt.

**Is this book part of a series?**
Yes, the description notes that *Palatul dorintei* creates an "horizon of anticipation for the next novel, *The Sugar Street*," suggesting it is part of a related literary cycle by Naguib Mahfouz.

**Who is the author/translator?**
While the original work is by Naguib Mahfouz, Paul E. Hutchinson is credited with bringing this story to the reader.
